gen-gf-gugi-fs-plein: Gugi's lowercase stands nearly as tall as its capitals. That tall, open-cut shape gives headings real presence, while Plein, a tidy sans, lets each round letter breathe with a clear channel leading in.
gen-gf-gugi-fs-roundo: Tall and sharply cut: Gugi's lowercase climbs nearly to cap height, with terminals cut open so the counters flow outward. Roundo, a quiet sans, keeps every small counter unclogged.
gen-gf-gugi-fs-spline-sans: Distinctive from the first glance, Gugi cuts its terminals open and lets its tall lowercase nearly touch the capitals. Spline Sans then keeps paragraphs moving, its wide curve gaps and matched strokes feeling friendly line after line.
gen-gf-gugi-fs-synonym: Synonym lays down a plain stripe of constant ink, with generous openings in every curve, dependable beneath Gugi. Gugi brings the tall, bold statement; Synonym carries the quiet reading.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-aclonica: Tall, bold, single-stroke lettering: Gugi keeps one stroke width throughout, terminals cut open. And Aclonica's sans lowercase, deep in the midsection with a mild thickness shift, gives Gugi's uniform line some variation beneath it.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-allerta: Gugi builds its uppercase from lines of one constant thickness, and its lowercase stands tall beside them. Allerta, a sans-serif with wide, loose tracking and a prominent x-height, would read in a relaxed, spread-out way over many lines.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-alumni-sans: Gugi has no stroke variation at all, just tall lowercase and open-cut terminals. Alumni Sans adds a mellow stroke contrast and a bracelet-wide c, which gives Gugi's uniform lines a gentle foil.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-alumni-sans-pinstripe: Tall and distinctive, Gugi cuts its terminals open so every counter flows outward. Alumni Sans Pinstripe packs a tight word texture beneath it, with rope-heavy curves and oversized lowercase beside small capitals.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-alumni-sans-sc: Distinctive from the start: Gugi's lowercase climbs nearly to cap height. Alumni Sans SC would settle into a dense, squeezed texture over many lines, with stems just outweighing hairlines and lowercase that towers beside its capitals.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-anaheim: Gugi traces every stroke at the width of a single stylus, and its lowercase climbs nearly to cap height. Anaheim's dense, rounded sans-serif forms give that line a low-contrast counterpart.
